recipes.name: Old-Fashioned Beef Stew
ingredients_raw: 1 pound lean beef chuck, trimmed and cut into 1 inch cubes
2 russet potatoes, sliced into 1/4 inch slices

steps.text: Coat beef with flour, shaking off excess. In a large nonstick stock pot, heat oil over medium-high heat, add beef and saute until brown, approximately 6 minutes. Remove beef from stock pot and set aside.
Add onions and mushrooms to stock pot and saute for 6 minutes. Add garlic and saute for 1 minute, continually stirring.

Skim off fat any fat from the stock pot and return cooked beef to pot; stir in tomato paste and broth. Add enough water to just cover ingredients and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low and simmer until beef is tender, about 1 hour and 15 minutes.
Skim off any foam that has accumulated on the surface of stew and add carrots, potatoes and green beans. Cover partially and simmer for 15 minutes.
In a small mixing bowl, mix cornstarch and cold water. Stir mixture into stew. Increase heat and boil uncovered for 1 minute. Sprinkle with parsley and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Old-Fashioned Beef Stew
raw_recipe.description: A traditional beef stew made from trimmed, lean beef chuck. This recipe includes potatoes, carrots, mushrooms, onions and green beans, and clear directions on how to eliminate unwanted fat from the stew.

review.reviewBody: I have used an identical recipe to this for some time now, and it really has 5-star potential. A few tips: I always add more tomato paste -- closer to 2 TBSP -- and stir it into the mixture before adding the broth. Also, the vegetables need extra time to cook at the end. Bring them to a boil and reduce heat to medium or med-high (still bubbling) and cook until veggies are just softened. Return to rapid boil for cornstarch addition and reduce heat to low or turn off completely. Add parsley and let sit for about 10 mins.-- the stew will reach a wonderful consistency. Serve with warm cornbread or rolls and you are set. Yummy!!!
Def. add spices, cook the veggies as long as the meat, add Way more broth and a full can of tomato paste. 😉

I enjoyed this recipe, it was simple and fast to make. I made it again, but this time I added a teaspoon of salt to the meat before I cooked it and instead of mushrooms, I used peas. Also had to cook longer so the carrots were properly cooked.

I made this recipe with a few variations. I cooked mine in a slow cooker for 8 hours. I used the listed vegetable suggestions and added a leftover bag of spinach leaves. I also used McCormicks Stew Beef seasoning pack. When the Stew is finished, I pour a bottle of 5 ounce Heinz 57 and let it heat to the temperature of the Stew. It has to be Heinz 57. No substitute allowed. We love it. Makes a fantastic winter stew/ soup.

I made this for Sunday night supper and it was so delicious! Hubby had seconds!! Great recipe. The small change I made was de-glazing the pan after browning the meat with beef stock and a bit of merlot. Super yummy!

I gave it a 4 cause I altered it a bit but my husband LOVED it. Using what I had in the house, I floured the beef w/ flour and Italian seasoning mix. I sautéed that in the oil and put them in the crock pot piece by piece with about 3 cups of beef broth. In the frying pan I simmered/softened about 2 cups of carrots diced, 1 large onion and 5-6 garlic cloves (no such thing as too many). Seasoned that w/ garlic powder, onion powder and black pepper and simmered with broth for about 20 minutes and dumped that in the pot. I added 2 chopped potatoes to the crock pot. I also added corn starch to thicken it. My hubby can't eat tomato stuff so omitted that. We didn't have mushrooms or green beans. OK, maybe I altered it A LOT but it was a good base to start with!

There was no seasoning in recipe. Obviously add salt and pepper as needed. Timing on potatoes, green beans and carrots are totally off. These don’t cook in 15 minutes as the recipe calls for. I put them in to allow for 35 minutes and still needed an additional 25 minutes. Need to look for other recipe or major doctoring requires.
Was bland, needed seasoning, even a shot of worchestershire sauce improved it.

I enjoyed the beef stew very flavorful, my husband lked it. I slow cooked for 8 hrs. On low, the meat I used 2 pounds of top sirloin steak which I put in flour, salt & pepper to season then put in pot whole. Sautéed the onion & mushroom and layed on top of mea then added the rest of the ingredients. I did change out the green bean to chopped celery. After the meal was ready it had the gravy look, but I add a beef bouillon for more flavor. I took the meat out which the meat was falling a part, I shredded the meat then put it back in pot. I would make this again

I browned my roast, sauteed my onions, added 1 package of Lipton beefy onion soup mix and added my broth. I always cook my vegetables separate as to not over cook them. Add any additional flavor you like. The soup mix makes it's own gravy.

This didn't have any herbs, etc. for flavor. Try tossing in a bay leaf! It pops! I toss in the left over flour from the meat to my softened onion and garlic for the gravy instead of corn starch. Tomato paste or sauce is up to you. Same with green beans.
Good. It needs salt and pepper and some kind of spice. Cooked the carrots and green beans longer for a soft but structured texture.

I made this recipe according to the instructions, with the exception of no green beans. It was good, but there is absolutely no indication of where or how much salt to add. I ended up adding 2 teaspoons at the end, but probably it could have used more, and added earlier in the process.
Delicious! I did add a pepper and a s-lash of garlic salt.

This is a great basic recipe for Old Fashioned Beef Stew. I did add and make some changes. I used 1 sliced onion, about one and a quarter pounds of chuck meat, I added 1 sliced parsnip, about 5 cloves of garlic and some red merlot wine, salt on the meat as it was sauted. I heated the beef broth and added the tomato paste to the warm beef broth. I also was short on time, so I added the vegetables and potatoes after about a half hour of simmering, then came back a half hour later and added the cornstarch, brought to a boil and simmered and extra 15 minutes. Since I did not have parsley, I served the stew with sprouts on top. It was delicious!

There were way too many carrots, otherwise good. I’m not a huge fan of carrots but partner is and he even said there were too many. He thought there should be more stew meat too. I’ll probably tweak next time since sauce flavor was good.
Just made this tonight for dinner and my husband and I loved it. The only change I made was to substitute frozen peas for the green beans. Otherwise, made it as written. This is a keeper.

No changes
